sections.title: 十二、阅读海报判断正误

sections.passage:
Tell Facts from Opinions
Do you know the difference between a fact and an opinion?
A fact is something that is true and can be proven. It can be checked or confirmed to be correct. For example, 'A year has twelve months.' This is a fact. We can easily check it in a calendar.
An opinion is what someone believes, thinks or feels. It cannot be proven true for everyone. Different people may hold different opinions. For example, 'Winter is the best season.' This is an opinion. Some people love winter, while others do not.
It is very important to tell facts from opinions when we read news, articles or stories. This helps us tell what is true from what someone simply believes. In this way, we are able to read wisely.

questions.explanation: 原文 'A fact is something that is true and can be proven.'，故为True。

questions.explanation: 原文 'Different people may hold different opinions.'，故为True。

questions.explanation: 原文明确指出这是一个观点（opinion），故为False。

questions.explanation: 原文说分清事实和观点都很重要，故为False。

questions.explanation: 原文 'we are able to read wisely.'，故为True。

sections.title: 十三、阅读文章 A

sections.passage:
Persuasion means making people agree with you. The Greeks had three easy ways to do it.
Ethos: Ethos wins people's trust. If you know a lot about something, others will believe you. For example, we listen to dentists about teeth. We also trust teachers when they talk about study.
Pathos: Pathos uses people's feelings. It makes people care and give help. For example, cute little dogs and cats can make people want to help them. Warm stories also move people.
Logos: Logos uses facts and numbers. Real facts make your words believable. For example, 'Apples have many vitamins' is a good fact.
People often use all three ways together. You can see them in speeches, advertisements and daily talks.

questions.explanation: 触及情感属于 pathos，选择B。
